summary: Turn 12. Map v3 was accepted, so I promoted the A7 client path from a bare Surface to real sourced objects and opened a correlation-duty Candidate. Map additions: B-CLIENT-ISSUE (Loop issues proposals to ClosestId, with the pipelining window), B-CLIENT-REPLY (WaitReplies/RegisterReply decodes ProposeReplyTS and carries its CommandId into ReqReply.Seqnum, so reply identity exists), B-CLIENT-OBSERVE (the Loop consumer reads c.Reply in arrival order, pairs the i-th reply with the i-th request for progress and latency, and the blocking Write/Read/Scan helpers return whichever reply arrives first, with the in-source TODO 'if the return value != i, something's wrong' at client/buffer.go:146-153), and F-CLIENT-REPLY-LINK as the assertion that a delivered reply is associated with the request that produced it (established by B-CLIENT-REPLY, consumed by B-CLIENT-OBSERVE). The previously unclassified Surface for this entry point moved to disposition 'mapped' with those behavior ids, and I supplied the corresponding map_changes clarification. Submitted action=continue with a new Candidate (disposition concrete_suspicion, preferred_check source_review, priority 1; activity_classes A7 with supported core activity A1 via the declared cross-activity effect; principal fact F-CLIENT-REPLY-LINK, direct behavior B-CLIENT-OBSERVE, supporting B-CLIENT-REPLY and B-CLIENT-ISSUE; obligation_relation_kind consumption). Its question asks whether the client must and does check that a reply answers a specific outstanding request, or whether a reply can be paired with the wrong request so a Read/Scan returns another request's value and completion is misattributed under pipelining. Counterevidence and unknowns keep it honest: the identity is preserved (used for latency indexing) rather than discarded, the non-pipelined default makes arrival order coincide with request order, and the open premises are whether the client contract requires the match and whether out-of-order replies are legal from a single ClosestId replica. Preflight validation returns valid=true; formal acceptance and any execution remain the controller's.
